packages.name: Arrange Footprints in Circle
packages.description: Place selected footprints evenly on a circle with live preview. No duplication, schematic links stay intact.
packages.description_full:
Moves the SELECTED footprints onto a circle (center = centroid of the selection). Nothing is duplicated, so every footprint keeps its schematic link (no "Update PCB from Schematic" conflicts).

Ideal for rings of serially-chained RGB LEDs or other circular part layouts.

Features:
- Live preview: each footprint is drawn as its pad bounding box, rotated according to the current settings
- Radius and start angle (0 deg = east, -90 deg = north/12 o'clock)
- Clockwise or counter-clockwise order (placement order = ascending reference)
- "Rotate parts": point each part's 0 deg direction radially outward
- "Keep silkscreen text upright": rotate parts but counter-rotate text on silkscreen layers so it stays readable (0/180 deg rule)
- Normal edit operation, undoable with Ctrl+Z

Usage: select the footprints in the PCB editor, then run Tools -> External Plugins -> Arrange Footprints in Circle.

packages.name: Arrange Mounting Holes
packages.description: Arrange selected mounting holes on a grid (columns x rows) with exact X/Y spacing. Live preview included.
packages.description_full:
Moves the SELECTED mounting-hole footprints onto a clean grid (columns x rows) with exact X/Y spacing, e.g. 4 holes on a 40 x 40 mm rectangle or 6 holes on a 2 x 3 grid. Nothing is duplicated and nothing is aligned to edge cuts — the holes are simply snapped to the grid positions of a centered rectangle.

Features:
- Live preview: grey dots are the holes' current positions, coloured boxes are the target grid points, each labelled with the reference that will land there
- Columns/Rows freely adjustable (defaults: factors closest to a square, oriented to the selection's bounding box)
- X/Y spacing in mm (defaults measured from the selection)
- Each hole moves to its nearest free grid point
- Optional: group the footprints after placing so they stay together as one movable unit (skipped automatically if they are already grouped)
- Normal edit operation, undoable with Ctrl+Z

Usage: select the mounting holes in the PCB editor, then run Tools -> External Plugins -> Arrange Mounting Holes.
